problem: Prior VLN agents (e.g. Ent-Rel) model objects and relations only in a loosely coupled latent space. They do not explicitly align instruction landmarks with visual objects, nor model agent-centric spatial relations such as 'table on your left'.
motivation: Agents rely on landmark and direction tokens, but it is hard to tell which landmarks matter at each step. Prior work picks landmarks mainly from visual context, ignoring instruction semantics, and focuses on motion direction words rather than landmark spatial descriptions. Explicit alignment would also make the agent's decisions more explainable.
key_idea: Split the instruction into spatial configurations, select the top-k landmarks by configuration attention, align them to the most similar Faster-RCNN objects, and align 6-bit textual and visual agent-centric spatial relation encodings to enrich candidate viewpoint features.
insight: Explicit landmark-object alignment gives gains over the Env-Drop baseline (val-unseen SR 0.47 to 0.50 for Lan-Obj), and adding agent-landmark relations gives more (0.52 SR, SDTW 0.37 to 0.46). Selecting k=3 landmarks is best; using 1 or all hurts. Relation modeling helps only when object alignment is correct: it hurts when objects such as scenes ('bathroom') are not detected, and the model is worse than Ent-Rel when scene tokens are included.
method: Spatial Configuration Representation: split the instruction into sub-instructions by verbs (following Zhang et al. 2021). Enrich each [SEP]-token representation with soft attention over the motion indicator and landmark GloVe embeddings; the decoder attends over configurations.
Landmark Selection: assign each configuration's attention weight to its landmarks, sort, and keep the top-k (k=3) landmarks at each step.

Landmark-Object Alignment: for each selected landmark, take the Faster-RCNN object (36 per image) with highest cosine similarity, and concatenate the aligned object features to the candidate image feature.

Landmark-Object Spatial Relation Alignment: extract landmark-relation pairs by syntactic rules, encode relations as a 6-bit vector [left, right, front, back, up, down], and derive the visual encoding from the relative angle to the agent's initial heading. The inner product of the two gives a similarity score, which is concatenated with the encodings to the candidate feature.

Action Prediction and Training: on the Env-Drop LSTM seq2seq base, the updated candidate features are scored against a context-aware hidden state with softmax. Training mixes IL and RL, and inference is greedy.

setting.backbone: Env-Drop LSTM seq2seq agent (BERT-base frozen embeddings + BiLSTM encoder, attentive LSTM decoder) with Faster-RCNN objects, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: R2R train set (no augmented data indicated for EXOR); IL+RL
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ResNet features) + Faster-RCNN object features (36 per view)

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (0.52 etc.) in the paper and are kept as printed, not converted to percent. NE, TL and OSR are not reported.
results: EXOR reaches val-unseen SR 0.52 / SPL 0.49 / SDTW 0.46 and test SR 0.49 / SPL 0.46, clearly above its Env-Drop base (0.47/0.43/0.37 val-unseen) and SpC-NAV. It roughly ties Ent-Rel on val-unseen (0.52/0.50/0.46), is below OAAM (0.54/0.50 SR/SPL), and is not SOTA versus pre-trained transformers.
limitations: Depends on Faster-RCNN detection, and relation modeling hurts when objects or scenes (e.g. 'bathroom') are not detected or are misaligned
Only models agent-landmark spatial relations, not landmark-landmark relations; the 6-bit encoding uses relative angle to the initial heading
Does not beat Ent-Rel or OAAM, and is below pre-trained transformer VLN models; evaluated on R2R only
